topology.host: single workstation, both instances and all dependencies on one machine
topology.rate_limit: capacity 100000 / 60s so the probe measures latency rather than throttle rejection

faults.observed: 12/12 requests across both instances still returned 200; rate limiting degraded to the in-memory bucket
faults.metric: parallax_ratelimit_degraded_total = 1 after the first failed Redis attempt

faults.action: kill the mysqld process on port 3307
faults.observed: authenticated read did not respond within a 15s client timeout, and /actuator/health was equally unresponsive; no fail-fast
faults.recovery: restart mysqld, next request 200 without restarting the gateway

limitations: Both instances and every dependency share one workstation; numbers are not a production capacity claim
Short burst only: no soak test, no ramp, no percentiles over a warmed JVM (p99 includes cold-start effects)
No load balancer or ingress in front; the probe alternates between instances itself
MySQL outage has no fail-fast or dedicated readiness signal, which is a real operational gap worth fixing
Data set is a single API key with a small ledger, so the query cost is not representative of a large tenant
